title: Guided free-form picking
thesis: With Level Up mode off, the level control shows a working level beside the character's level — the next empty pick slot, or a clicked one — powers out of reach at the working level are dimmed but still pickable, an empty pick slot can be clicked to target it, and a power held without its prerequisite at an earlier level is marked until the build is put back in order.
body:
Free-form (Level Up mode off) is the default and stays free: nothing is refused for being early
or out of order. It guides instead, the way Mids' Reborn does outside its own level-up mode.
Level Up mode stays the strict option and is not changed by this work.

Decisions (2026-10-10, user-chosen):
- The level that follows the picks is a separate *working level*, shown beside the character's
  level as `50 (14)`. `CharacterState::level` stays what the user set and still drives totals,
  slot budget and inherents. The working level drives only dimming and where the next pick goes.
  Once every pick is filled the control shows just `50`.
  Rejected: moving `CharacterState::level` itself (chosen earlier the same day, then replaced by
  the user — totals and the slot budget would shift with every pick).
- The working level is computed from the build (earliest empty pick slot), so it is not saved
  and adds no undo steps. Only a clicked slot is held, as temporary UI state.
- A pick above the current level lands in the earliest empty slot it can legally fill. This is
  already what `next_pick_level` does.
- Prerequisites come from the power's `requires` expression in the contract, the same data that
  gates picks today. No hand-written table.
- Only a missing or out-of-order prerequisite raises the warning. It shows in two places: on the
  power's card in the by-level grid, and as a red italic name in the power list (Mids shows only
  the latter).
- Clicking an empty pick slot sets the working level to that slot's level (Mids' behaviour).
  After the next pick it returns to the earliest empty slot.
- Level Up mode keeps refusing a pick whose prerequisite is missing.

## Preconditions

- `main` builds and `cargo nextest run --workspace` passes before work starts.
- The homecoming contract carries `requires` on pool powers — checked 2026-10-10:
  `Pool.Fighting.Tough` has `["Pool.Fighting.Boxing","Pool.Fighting.Kick","||"]`.

## Out of scope

- The by-powerset layout of the Powers panel: it has no empty slots to click. The working level
  still shows there (guided-picking-3).
- Any change to Level Up mode beyond keeping its refusal (guided-picking-2).
- Fixing an out-of-order build automatically. The planner marks it; the user reorders.
- Any change to how `CharacterState::level` is set. The user's level control works as before.
- Order checks on enhancement slot levels. This plan is about power picks only.
- Set-level gates (`PoolDef.buy_requires`, epic `minLevel`): they are level rules, which
  placement already honours.

title: Layout follows the account
thesis: A signed-in player's layout is saved to their account automatically and comes back on any browser or device they sign in on, the most recently edited copy winning, while a signed-out player sees no change at all.
body:
Player feedback, 2026-10-01: building a dashboard is many clicks and drags, and it is lost
on a new browser, a new device, or a cleared cache. Today every part of the layout lives only
in that browser's `localStorage`. The live site was checked the same day: a layout does
survive a reload, so the loss is where it is kept, not a save bug.

"Layout" here means exactly five stored keys, no more:

| key | what it holds | written by |
|---|---|---|
| `sk-stats-config` | the stat panels, their names and their stats | [stats_store.rs](../crates/app/src/stats_store.rs) |
| `sk-layout` | each panel's place on the desktop grid, one slot per column count | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |
| `sk-mobile-order` | the order of panels on a phone | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |
| `sk-quickbar` | the pinned quickbar buttons | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |
| `sk-powers-layout` | the Powers panel's by-powerset / by-level view | [layout_store.rs](../crates/app/src/layout_store.rs) |

Decisions, 2026-10-01, user-chosen:

- **Layout only.** Rejected: also theme, UI size and alert settings (more to test, and UI
  size arguably belongs to the device); stat panels only (grid positions would still be lost).
- **Newest edit wins**, whole layout against whole layout. Rejected: account always wins
  (overwrites a layout built before signing in, silently); asking the player (a dialog to
  design for a case the timestamp already answers).
  Amended 2026-10-01 after the first signed-in test (user-chosen): newest wins only between
  copies of the same account's layout. A layout edited signed out, or under another account,
  loses to the account's copy at sign-in, and an account with no copy yet takes the browser's.
  Found when panels hidden while signed out overwrote the account's copy on signing back in.
- **Saved automatically**, a moment after the last change. Rejected: a save button
  (players forget, which is the failure being fixed).

The server is the Supabase project the beta also uses. Its schema lives in the beta's repo,
`~/Github/CoH-Sidekick/supabase/schema.sql`, and changes reach the live database as a
migration file pasted into the SQL editor. The `favorites` table (schema.sql:517) is the
pattern: one user's rows, readable and writable only by that user, written straight from the
client with no edge function.

## Preconditions

Checked 2026-10-01:

- The beta repo `~/Github/CoH-Sidekick` has a clean working tree.
- The client can already select and upsert table rows: `Cloud::select` and `Cloud::upsert`
  in [cloud/mod.rs](../crates/app/src/cloud/mod.rs).
- Sign-in already triggers a per-user fetch (favorites) at
  [account.rs:261](../crates/app/src/cloud/account.rs#L261), which is where the layout
  fetch joins.

Not checkable from here, and assumed: sign-in works on next.coh-sidekick.com and in the
desktop build, and the live database matches `schema.sql`.

## Out of scope

- **Theme, UI size, alerts and other display preferences.** Decided out above; a later plan
  can add keys to the same document once this one works.
- **Live sync between two open tabs.** The other tab picks up the change on its next load.
  Pushing changes into an open page is a separate, larger feature.
- **Merging two layouts.** Newest wins whole. A merge has no right answer for a panel moved
  in both copies.
- **The build itself (`sk-build`).** Builds already save to the account their own way.
- **Layout history or undo.** One copy per account.
- **The beta reading this table.** It is written for this app; the beta never sees it.

title: The Linux AppImage starts on any distribution
thesis: The release workflow's Linux AppImage opens its window on a clean Ubuntu and a clean Fedora, using WebKit helper programs it carries itself, and the workflow refuses to upload one that cannot.
body:
Found 2026-10-17. The v1.0.0-rc1 Linux AppImage (run 39064054571, sha256 5a2dd428…) exits at
once on the owner's Fedora 44 KDE desktop:

    Failed to spawn child process "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/webkit2gtk-4.1/WebKitNetworkProcess"

The AppImage carries `libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0` from the Ubuntu runner but none of WebKit's
helper programs (WebKitNetworkProcess, WebKitWebProcess, the injected bundle). The library has
Ubuntu's helper folder compiled in, so on any system that keeps them elsewhere it cannot start.
On a system that does have them there, it would run the host's helpers against its own library,
which breaks the moment the versions differ — the September Fedora-built AppImage showed exactly
that ("Received invalid message" against Fedora's 2.54 helpers with a bundled 2.52.5). The
release workflow reported success because nothing in it ever starts the app.

Decision, 2026-10-17, owner: option 1 of three offered — carry the helpers inside the AppImage
and point the library at them, the approach Tauri ships. Rejected: leaving WebKit out and using
the system's (fails on desktops without WebKit, which includes KDE installs), and a Flatpak (a
different install story).

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-17:
- the bundled library names exactly two helper paths, `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/webkit2gtk-4.1`
  and its `injected-bundle/`, read with `strings` from the rc1 AppImage.
- the AppImage's AppRun is the app binary itself (no linuxdeploy GTK plugin, no hooks), so a
  launcher has to be added rather than edited.
- podman is installed, with `registry.fedoraproject.org/fedora:41` and an Ubuntu noble image
  (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`) local, so both targets can be run here.

Out of scope:
- Flatpak, .deb and .rpm packages: a different install story, decided against above.
- Starting the Windows and macOS builds in CI: their own problem, with no evidence yet that they
  fail; this plan is about the Linux file.
- Code signing, update checks and publishing the rc1 draft: publishing waits on this plan, but is
  the owner's act, not an item here.
- ARM Linux: no one has asked for it, and the workflow builds x86_64 only.

evidence: scripts/keys/rc-appimage-launch.sh run 2026-10-17 against rc1 (sha256 5a2dd428…): exit 1 on ubuntu:24.04 and fedora:44, both with "Failed to spawn child process /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/webkit2gtk-4.1/WebKitNetworkProcess". The containers carry GTK 3, Mesa with GLES and fonts, and no WebKit; the first two runs failed on missing libfribidi and libGLESv2 instead, which is why those are installed.

rc-appimage-webkit.sh run on rc1 in ubuntu:24.04 (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 2.52.6, build ID 6d0db877… equal to the bundled one): 3 helper programs and the injected bundle carried, 2 helper paths rewritten. rc-appimage-launch.sh then PASSes on ubuntu:24.04 and fedora:44, and both screenshots show the planner with its Welcome dialog. Two findings on the way: linuxdeploy rewrites bundled libraries, so the build match is by build ID, not bytes; and Ubuntu libwayland-client loaded on Fedora made Mesa EGL refuse and the page process abort behind an empty window, so the four libwayland libraries are now left to the host. The working directory moves to $APPDIR/usr; nothing in crates/app reads it.

title: Icons for archetypes, origins and powersets
thesis: The four build identity menus (Origin, Archetype, Primary, Secondary) show the game's icon beside every choice, in the closed menu and in its open list, and every build card in the build browser shows the build's archetype, primary and secondary icons.
body:
Asked 2026-10-18 by a player, who colour-matches origins to archetypes (Controllers and Dominators show pink, so they play them Mutation) and wants the icons in the identity menus. The owner added: also put archetype, primary and secondary icons on the build cards.

Decided 2026-10-18, owner:
- The menus become our own dropdown, not the browser's built-in one, because a built-in menu can only show text. Rejected: an icon beside a text-only menu (the open list stays text, so colours can't be compared while picking), and origin as five icon buttons.
- Powerset icons are the game's own set icons, taken from the game archives. Rejected: Mids' images, and the first power's icon as a stand-in.

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-18:
- Archetype icons: present. The game's own `archetypeicon_*.tga` / `v_archetypeicon_*.tga` (32x32 PNG data) are in `crates/app/assets/img/powers/` for all 15 playable archetypes; `assets/img/Archetypes/Class_*.png` also exists. No code uses either yet.
- Origin icons: present, `crates/app/assets/img/Origins/{Magic,Mutation,Natural,Science,Technology}.png`.
- Powerset icon names: present in game data. The bin crawler reads them from the powers bin (`export_powers.py:771`), e.g. `fire_blast_set.ico`, and every contract powerset carries one in `icon`. `coh_data::Powerset` has no typed field for it; it sits in `extra`.
- Powerset icon pictures: NOT FOUND. None of the 98 archives in `~/coh_piggs_merged` (Issue 24 and Homecoming beta) holds a `*_set` texture or any per-set art, and no other `.pigg` or `*_set.ico` exists on this disk. identity-icons-2 needs a current Homecoming client's archives first.
- The build card is one component, `BuildCard` in `cloud/browser.rs`, used by the browse grid, the favourites grid, My Builds and the author modal. Its summary carries archetype, primary and secondary ids, and no origin.

Out of scope:
- The other built-in menus (cloud browse filters, powerset compare, set bonus finder): not part of the request; the new dropdown can be reused there later.
- Origin on the build cards: the shared-build summary does not carry origin, and the owner's note names archetype and the two sets only.
- The exported build image (Export as Image and the share preview): a separate picture, not the browser's cards.
- Pool and epic pool pickers: not identity menus.

A powerset whose icon file is missing returns nothing, so the caller shows no picture instead of a broken one.

body:
Asked 2026-10-18 by a player, who colour-matches origins to archetypes (Controllers and Dominators show pink, so they play them Mutation) and wants the icons in the identity menus. The owner added: also put archetype, primary and secondary icons on the build cards.

Decided 2026-10-18, owner:
- The menus become our own dropdown, not the browser's built-in one, because a built-in menu can only show text. Rejected: an icon beside a text-only menu (the open list stays text, so colours can't be compared while picking), and origin as five icon buttons.
- Powerset icons: at first the game's own set icons from the archives. Revised the same day once the client turned out to have none: a set borrows the icon of its earliest player-picked power (identity-icons-2), and a better rule from the game's icon naming stays open (identity-icons-8). Rejected: Mids' set images, which are Mids' own invention.

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-18:
- Archetype icons: present. The game's own `archetypeicon_*.tga` / `v_archetypeicon_*.tga` (32x32 PNG data) are in `crates/app/assets/img/powers/` for all 15 playable archetypes; `assets/img/Archetypes/Class_*.png` also exists. No code uses either yet.
- Origin icons: present, `crates/app/assets/img/Origins/{Magic,Mutation,Natural,Science,Technology}.png`.
- Powerset icon names: present in game data. The bin crawler reads them from the powers bin (`export_powers.py:771`), e.g. `fire_blast_set.ico`, and every contract powerset carries one in `icon`. `coh_data::Powerset` has no typed field for it; it sits in `extra`.
- Powerset icon pictures: do not exist. The Homecoming client at `~/.wine/drive_c/Games/Homecoming` (173 archives, 93,655 entries, plus loose files) has none of the 126 set icon names the data carries; its `gui/icons` has archetype and origin folders and no powerset one.
- The build card is one component, `BuildCard` in `cloud/browser.rs`, used by the browse grid, the favourites grid, My Builds and the author modal. Its summary carries archetype, primary and secondary ids, and no origin.

Out of scope:
- The other built-in menus (cloud browse filters, powerset compare, set bonus finder): not part of the request; the new dropdown can be reused there later.
- Origin on the build cards: the shared-build summary does not carry origin, and the owner's note names archetype and the two sets only.
- The exported build image (Export as Image and the share preview): a separate picture, not the browser's cards.
- Pool and epic pool pickers: not identity menus.

says: Granite Armor Defense debuff resistance rises with slotted Defense enhancement; the game holds it flat.
body: Reported by a user 2026-10-24 on a Tanker Stone Armor build: defense enhancement within granite is increasing the resistance number within sidekick but not in game. apply.rs pass 2b multiplied the defense type of debuff resistance by (1 + enh.get(defense)), ported from the beta debuffResEnhMapping (legacy-totals.oracle.ts:837); Mids Reborn agrees (GBPA_Pass1_EnhancePreED routes ResEffect/ETModifies==Defense onto eEnhance.Defense, clsToonX.cs:1798). Both are wrong. Owner measured Homecoming test server 2026-10-24: L50 Tanker, Granite ON, DDR = 43.25% at 0,1,2,3,4,5,6 slotted L50 Defense IOs; 0.00 with Granite OFF. The unslotted 43.25 is scale 1.0 x Tanker melee_res_boolean[50], so the AT-table read is right and only the multiplier is wrong. The data agrees once the right token is asked: a DDR row is Base_Defense aspect=Resistance, its boost token is Debuff_Defense, and across all four datasets 1168 powers carry a DDR row, 2373 allow Debuff_Defense, overlap exactly zero. The 118 DDR powers listing Buff_Defense mean their positional defense BUFF rows enhance, not the DDR row.

evidence: apply.rs apply_debuff_resistance: dropped enh_multiplier, so every debuff-resistance type resolves as resolve_scaled_effect x 100 with no enhancement; the block comment now records DDR-1 (beta debuffResEnhMapping, Mids GBPA_Pass1_EnhancePreED, the measured flat ladder, the zero-overlap census). New tests/debuff_resistance_not_enhanced.rs: granite_defense_ddr_ignores_defense_enhancement walks 0..6 Defense IOs over all four forks and asserts the number never moves off 43.25; granite_positional_defense_still_takes_defense_enhancement asserts the same powers Smashing defense still goes 15 -> 25.49, so a fix that zeroed the whole defense aspect could not pass. Broke it on purpose: with the multiplier restored the first test fails at Homecoming, 1 IO moving 43.25000047683716 to 54.25712567037344; the second still passes. Full nextest 245/245, lint:rust clean, fmt:rust:check clean, baseline:check holds every field of all 143 builds across the four datasets. In-app Q/A on the rebuilt web bundle (dx serve --platform web, port 8787): loaded fixtures/qa/granite-ddr-probe.skif (L50 Tanker, Stone Armor / Super Strength, Granite ON, 6x L50 Defense IO), Detailed Totals Debuff Resistance Defense reads 43.25%, breakdown Active Powers Granite Armor +43.25%, Total +43.25% — matching the test server. The Defense panel still reads Melee 0% / Ranged 0%: Granite grants Smashing/Lethal Build Defense, which the panel hides by default, so that is unchanged and correct.

says: Defense Debuff Resistance has no display cap; Mids clamps it at 95%. Which is right is unmeasured.
done_when: Owner reads Defense Debuff Resistance on the Homecoming test server for the fixtures/qa/ddr-cap-probe.skif build (L50 Tanker, Super Reflexes / Super Strength, all seven DDR toggles on) and reports whether the game shows 121.1 or clamps it, and to what.
body: Mids caps the DDR display at Statistics.MaxDefenseDebuffRes = 95f (Core/Statistics.cs:20), applied with Math.Min in Core/StatsPowerData.cs and the totals window; Sidekick has cap: StatCap::None on stat_registry debuff_defense and no clamp in finalize.rs. The granite fix (unfiled-3) tops out at 43.25 so it cannot show the difference. A build that clears 95 exists: every tanker DDR source is in a PRIMARY-only set, and Super Reflexes carries seven DDR powers with no toggle exclusivity between them, so all seven stack. Measured 121.1% (Elude 43.25 + Evasion/Focused Fighting/Focused Senses 17.3 each + Agile/Dodge/Lucky 8.65 each), in the engine and in the web app on fixtures/qa/ddr-cap-probe.skif. No power pool or epic pool in Homecoming carries a Defense aspect=Res atom, so pools add nothing to DDR - the earlier guess that Leadership did was wrong, its Defense atoms are aspect=Cur buffs on teammates. Whether 95 is a real game cap or a Mids display convention is unknown; do not add a clamp until the test server says.

says: Whether a Defense IO moves Defense Debuff Resistance may be decided per row by IgnoreStrength, not for every DDR row at once as unfiled-3 made it.
done_when: Owner reads Defense Debuff Resistance on the Homecoming test server for a L50 Super Reflexes character with Focused Fighting on, at 0 and at 3 L50 Defense IOs in Focused Fighting, and reports whether it moves (engine reads 17.30 flat since unfiled-3; 1 + Defense enhancement would put it near 27).
body: Found 2026-10-24 by a coh-rc1bench b05 run, which also removed the DDR Defense multiplier from buff_pets.rs:283 (enh_multiplier, the pet mirror unfiled-3 left in place). Census of exported_powers (Homecoming): of 421 player-set DDR rows (attribs Base_Defense, aspect Resistance) 365 carry the IgnoreStrength flag and 56 do not; pets/redirects 36 and 2. Granite's DDR row (tanker_defense/stone_armor/granite_armor.json) IS flagged IgnoreStrength, so the flat test-server ladder in unfiled-3 is what the flag predicts and cannot tell the flag rule from the no-DDR-is-enhanced rule. Unflagged rows: Super Reflexes agile, dodge, elude, enduring, evasion, focused_fighting, focused_senses, lucky; Shield Defense battle_agility, deflection; Psionic Armor precognition; Empathy fortitude; Sonic Resonance sonic_siphon; Teamwork foresight; Sun Xiong and supersoldier sets; and both buff-pets, Force Field Dampening Bubble (redirects/force_field/dampening_bubble.json) and Light Affinity Prismatic Shield (sanctuarypatch_sanctuaryaura.json). Both pets are CopyBoosts and allow Buff_Defense; in the engine today 3 Defense IOs raise their DDR (Force Bubble on a Controller 17.30 -> 27.41, Sanctuary of Light 34.60 -> 54.82, Homecoming and Brainstorm; Rebirth and Thunderspy carry neither). If the test server shows Focused Fighting moving, unfiled-3 over-reached for the 56 unflagged rows and the pet line is right; if flat, the pet line is the leftover and should go, as the b05 run did. Also bears on unfiled-4: the 121.1 SR stack is built entirely from unflagged rows.

evidence: Settled from the game files, not the test server: each archetype ResistanceMaxTable in classes.bin carries the debuff-resistance ceilings, identical on Homecoming, Brainstorm, Rebirth and Thunderspy (all 15 player ATs each, read 2026-10-27). Defense, to-hit, recovery and regeneration rise from 20% at L1 to 95% at L47, matching the Homecoming wiki Limits table; endurance rises 2/level to 95% at L39; Controller/Dominator/Mastermind regeneration stops at 47.5%; slow, recharge and perception are 100%. The exporter now writes these rows (debuff_resistance_cap), the contract carries debuffResistanceCapTable, and finalize clamps each row to its own ceiling. The SR stack (121.1 raw) shows 95 at L50 and 59.36 at L25 on Rebirth and Thunderspy in the web app; tests/debuff_resistance_caps.rs pins the tables on all four forks and fails with endurance pointed at the defense row.

says: Shopping-list progress survives across sessions: enhancement-list ticks live on the build, and a saved .skif file carries both lists' progress.
done_when: In the web app, ticking enhancement-list rows and incarnate shopping-list salvage, reloading the page, and opening a .skif saved from that build all show the same ticks; Reset clears them; a build posted to the shared repository carries none. Tests pin the .skif round trip and the share strip.
body: Reported by a user 2026-10-29: shopping lists are not persisting. Enhancement-list ticks were modal-local by design (enhancement_list.rs module doc), which misread the owner: buying and crafting runs over several sessions, so ticks must be cached, clearable and saved with the build. Incarnate shopping progress (shopping_acquired, crafting_obtained, crafting_salvage_checked) already rides the localStorage autosave, but skif::slim never wrote them, so Save to file dropped them. The beta wrote its three into files and stripped them only from share links (build-serialization.ts:119, :140).

evidence: CharacterState::enhancement_acquired holds the enhancement-list ticks; the modal reads and writes it through BuildSession::commit, so each tick is an undo step and the localStorage autosave keeps it. Rows are keyed by purchase_key (set id + piece, generic stat, special id, origin tier + stat, then level, attuned, boost), not display names. SkifBuild gains an optional progress block (enhancements, incarnateSalvage, crafted, salvageChecked); skif::encode writes it, encode_shared drops it and save_build::build_envelope uses that for the shared repository and short links. The v2-v4 reader re-keys the beta shoppingListAcquired onto S_ salvage ids from the catalog, reports unknown ids, and says the beta crafted-node ticks were left out. Tests: tests/shopping_progress_travels.rs (file round trip, share strip, beta counts) and enhancement_list::tests::a_tick_finds_its_row_after_a_save_and_reopen; the first two fail with the encode/decode lines disabled, the key test fails with display names in the key. nextest 290/290, lint:rust and fmt:rust:check clean. Web Q/A on charnel.txt with Alpha C. Paragon: ticked 2 Aegis pieces and 1 Arcane Cantrip -> Pieces 93/95, Catalysts 57/59, Arcane Cantrip (1/3); same after page reload; Save to file wrote progress {enhancements: 2, incarnateSalvage: S_ArcaneCantrip 1}; that file opened in a fresh browser showed 93/95 and (1/3) again; Reset ticks -> Pieces 95, Reset acquired -> 3 x Arcane Cantrip, 440 Threads. Not checked in the app: the shared-repository strip (needs sign-in; covered by the share test).

says: A private cloud save carries the owner's shopping progress, and no build that anyone else can read ever does.
done_when: Saving a build as Private in the cloud and loading it back from My Builds restores both shopping lists' ticks. Public, unlisted and short-link saves send none. body: Follows unfiled-6, which kept progress out of every cloud save because the server can flip a private row public (update-build-visibility) without the build passing back through the client. Server-side removal mirrors the F08 preview rule (_shared/preview-visibility.ts): one predicate, fail closed on an unknown visibility. The client sends progress only when the dialog's chosen visibility is Private; a stale target visibility is covered by share-build stripping on the effective visibility.

evidence: Client: save_build::keeps_progress sends progress only for a Private save; quick share and public/unlisted saves use encode_shared. tests: only_a_private_save_carries_the_shopping_progress (fails with keeps_progress always true). Server (coh-sidekick-beta d591be2c6a): _shared/build-progress.ts progressMayStay + withoutProgress, applied in share-build (insert and update, on the effective visibility) and update-build-visibility (only rewrites build_json when progress was present); build-progress.test.ts 7 tests, source guards fail with either call removed; supabase vitest 191/191; app nextest 291/291, lint and fmt clean. share-build and update-build-visibility deployed to utnqoueoiixygoqerfiw on 2026-10-29 before the app change. Owner ran the signed-in round trip on 2026-10-29 against a local build and reported that it works; the individual readings were not reported.

title: Convert a build to another archetype
thesis: A build can be copied to another archetype: every power set the two archetypes share comes across with its picks and slotting, at levels the new archetype allows, and everything that could not come across is listed before the copy is made.
body:
Decided 2026-10-30, owner (in conversation):
- Conversion makes a new copy; the original build is untouched, so the two can be compared.
- A set the new archetype lacks is left empty for the player to pick (Blaster to Defender keeps the blast set as the secondary; the primary is empty).
- Powers are matched by name inside a shared set, so per-archetype variants (Stalker, Tanker, Sentinel) come across where names agree and are listed where they don't.
- Slots on powers that could not come across go back to the slot pool.
- The player sees a report (kept, moved, dropped) and confirms before the copy is made.

Which sets two archetypes share comes from the archetype rosters the identity menu already uses (powerset_options in crates/app/src/powerset_compare.rs), not a hand-written table.

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-30:
- Changing archetype today clears every set-dependent pick (set_archetype, crates/app/src/panels/identity.rs:207). Conversion is a separate path; that behaviour stays.
- Each archetype's selectable sets are listed by powerset_options.

Out of scope:
- Suggesting replacements for enhancements that cannot follow (archetype-only sets such as Blaster's Wrath): they are listed, not swapped.
- Kheldians and the Arachnos archetypes: they share no sets with anyone.
- Converting between datasets (Homecoming to Rebirth): a different problem about which powers exist at all.

says: When a carried-over power can't be taken at its old level any more, decide whether conversion moves it to the next level that allows it or leaves it out and lists it.
body: Happens whenever a set changes position: a blast set as a Defender's secondary unlocks its powers later than as a Blaster's primary. Agent's recommendation (2026-10-30): move it to the next legal level and say so in the report, since dropping a power the player chose is the worse surprise.

says: A conversion function copies a build to a target archetype, keeping each shared power set in its new primary or secondary position with the same picks and slotting, matched by power name.
done_when: Tests cover four pairs: Scrapper to Brute (both sets, same positions), Tanker to Brute (both sets, swapped), Blaster to Defender (blast becomes the secondary, primary empty), and Scrapper to Stalker (powers with no same-named match are reported, not guessed). The original build is unchanged after each.

says: Carried-over picks land at levels the new archetype allows, following the rule archetype-conversion-1 decides.
done_when: A test converts a level-50 Blaster with its blast nuke taken at 32 to a Defender: the copy has no pick below the level its set position allows, and the report names every pick that moved or dropped.

says: The conversion report lists everything that could not come across: the epic pool, the inherents, powers with no match, and enhancements the new archetype or the new power cannot hold.
done_when: A test converts a Blaster slotted with Blaster's Wrath and an epic pool to a Defender, and the report names the Blaster's Wrath pieces, the epic pool and the Blaster-only inherent. Regular power pools and Incarnate powers come across and are not listed.

says: The planner offers Convert to another archetype: the player picks one, reads the report, confirms, and a new build opens with its empty set marked.
done_when: In the web app (qa-check), a Blaster build converted to Defender shows the report first; after confirming, a new build opens with the blast set as the secondary, the primary waiting to be picked, and the freed slots back in the slot pool, and the original Blaster build is still there unchanged. Converting a Scrapper to a Brute carries both sets with nothing listed as dropped.

title: Show how close each power is to the ED caps
thesis: Every slotted power shows, for each aspect it enhances, how much is slotted, how much counts after Enhancement Diversification, which stage of diminishing returns it has reached, and what one more enhancement of that aspect would add, with numbers that agree with the build's totals.
body:
Asked for 2026-10-30, owner: a feature the planner is missing that Mids has, where colour shows the point past which more slotting adds very little.

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-30:
- The engine already sums each power's raw enhancement per aspect, then applies ED once per aspect (calculate_power_enhancement_bonuses and apply_ed_per_aspect, crates/coh_math/src/enhancement.rs). Only the after-ED value leaves it; accumulate_raw_io_bonuses is private. So enhancement-caps-2 is new engine surface, not a recomputation in the UI.
- The Alpha incarnate is combined with ED in its own step (combine_with_alpha_ed). The breakdown must go through the same path or its numbers will disagree with the totals.

Out of scope:
- Global bonuses (set bonuses, LotG's +Recharge): they are not under ED, so they don't belong on a per-power cap display.
- Suggesting where to move a slot: this shows the numbers; deciding is the player's.
- Comparing two slottings side by side: compare_slotting.rs already covers that.

says: Decide where the ED breakdown shows (on the power card, in its tooltip, or both), the colours for each stage, and what one more enhancement means.
body: Agent's proposal (2026-10-30): a small stage mark per aspect on the card, the full numbers in the tooltip; one more enhancement means a level-50 single-aspect IO of that aspect. Colours should follow the stages Mids users already know, within the hues this app already spends on stat families.

title: Find sets from the bonus you want
thesis: A player chasing a particular set bonus can work from the bonus instead of from each power: the slot picker can narrow its sets to those granting a chosen bonus or any tracked stat, and the set bonus finder can list the build's own powers that could carry that bonus, what each would cost in slots, and whether the rule of five still lets it count.
body:
Decided 2026-10-30, owner (in conversation). While slotting for Energy and Negative Energy resistance, the owner kept opening power after power and reading their sets to find which ones carried those bonuses. The three questions that fit:
- In the slot picker: which set can go in this power and give me this bonus? (bonus-hunting-2)
- Is this bonus still doing anything, or do I already have five? (bonus-hunting-3)
- Where in my build can I fit another copy of this bonus? (bonus-hunting-4; the one the owner kept asking)
And, separately: an option to show only sets that match the tracked stats (bonus-hunting-1).

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-30:
- The picker's facets (set type, rarity, size, procs only, craftable level) are a pure filter in crates/app/src/picker_sets.rs (SetFacets), with a count on each facet button. New filters belong there.
- The picker already tags each set with its bonuses to tracked stats (set_tracked_bonuses, crates/app/src/tracked_stats.rs) and strikes through a bonus the build already holds five of (crates/app/src/panels/powers.rs, around line 937).
- The set bonus finder already files every bonus under the stat it moves, and knows which set categories the build's powers accept (slottable_categories, crates/app/src/panels/set_bonus_finder.rs). bonus-hunting-4 regroups that by power.

Out of scope:
- Ranking sets by how far they move the build toward stated targets ("45% ranged defense"): a bigger feature that can build on this one.
- Unique pieces' global effects (LotG +Recharge, Steadfast +Defense): they are not set bonuses, and the finder already records why they are missing.
- Powers not yet taken: bonus-hunting-4 lists the build's own powers only.
- Slotting anything automatically: every result is a suggestion the player acts on.

Level 1 holds only picks already there (character creation); a power the game hands out (level 0) holds no pick and is left alone. title: Carry archetype sets across a conversion
thesis: Converting a build to another archetype turns each archetype set (ATO) piece into the matching piece of the new archetype's own set, instead of emptying the slot: the same position among the archetype's two sets, the same tier (regular or Superior), the same piece number, so the result is uniform and predictable.
body:
Asked for 2026-10-30, owner, after trying the conversion on sonic-kinetic-tank.skif (Tanker with six Superior Might of the Tanker and six Superior Gauntleted Fist pieces). Decided 2026-10-30, owner (in conversation):
- Sets pair by a fixed order, first with first and second with second, not by name or bonus similarity.
- Pieces pair by piece number, 1 to 6, for a uniform and predictable mapping; where the new piece enhances a different mix, the report says which piece it became.

The order is the game's own: boostsets.bin lists each archetype's two sets in a fixed order (Tanker: Might of the Tanker, then Gauntleted Fist; Brute: Brute's Fury, then Unrelenting Fury; Scrapper: Scrapper's Strike, then Critical Strikes; Blaster: Blaster's Wrath, then Defiant Barrage; Defender: Defender's Bastion, then Vigilant Assault). That order happens to pair the sets with the closest bonuses too. It is lost today: the io-sets section is keyed and sorted by set id.

Preconditions, checked 2026-10-30:
- exported_powers/boostsets.json holds the bin order; scripts/extract-rebirth-io-sets-v2.py builds the io-sets section from it (build_sets), and some Homecoming entries are reused from the hand file (_reuse_hand_entry).
- IoSet (crates/coh_data/src/io_sets.rs) has no deny_unknown_fields, so a new field decodes as absent on an older bundle.
- A Superior set's rarity is ECSATO, a regular one ECATO; type is '<Archetype> Archetype Sets'.

Out of scope:
- Choosing the pairing in the dialog: the owner chose a fixed rule.
- Unique-piece conflicts beyond the power itself: an ATO proc is unique, but each archetype's sets are its own, so a converted proc cannot meet another copy from outside the conversion.

says: Each IO set in the contract carries its position in the game's boostsets.bin, so code can tell an archetype's first set from its second.
done_when: After npm run regen, every archetype set in the Homecoming io-sets section carries the position, Might of the Tanker's below Gauntleted Fist's and Brute's Fury's below Unrelenting Fury's; IoSet reads it as an Option, absent on a bundle without it; a second regen leaves the tree clean.

says: convert_build turns each archetype set piece into the new archetype's set at the same position and tier, same piece number, keeping attuned, level and booster, and the report names each set it turned into and any piece whose enhancement mix changed.
done_when: A test converts sonic-kinetic-tank.skif's pieces as a fixture (Tanker, Superior Might of the Tanker and Superior Gauntleted Fist) to Brute: the copy holds Superior Brute's Fury and Superior Unrelenting Fury at the same piece numbers in the same powers, none emptied; Blaster to Defender maps Superior Blaster's Wrath to Superior Defender's Bastion and reports pieces 3 and 4 as different mixes; a set with no counterpart (no position, or a target with fewer sets) is still emptied and listed.

says: The conversion report shows converted archetype sets as their own section, and the copy in the app holds the new sets.
done_when: In the web app (qa-check), sonic-kinetic-tank.skif converted to Brute shows 'Might of the Tanker becomes Brute's Fury' style lines and no ATO pieces under taken out; after converting, the powers that held Tanker pieces show the Brute set's pieces.

evidence: scripts/extract-rebirth-io-sets-v2.py stamps binOrder (the set's index in boostsets.json, the lossless round trip of boostsets.bin) on every set in a final pass after all override passes, since several replace whole entries; the shape comment documents it. IoSet (crates/coh_data/src/io_sets.rs) reads it as bin_order: Option<u32>, serde default, so an older bundle decodes as absent. npm run regen: the io-sets diff in all four contracts is 227/233/213/227 binOrder insertions and nothing else, every set carries one; Homecoming Might of the Tanker 178, Superior 179, Gauntleted Fist 180, Superior 181, Brute's Fury 186/187, Unrelenting Fury 188/189. A second regen left every io-sets.json and bundle byte-identical (md5). totals_baseline then reported the bundle fingerprint moved with no build or field differing; npm run baseline:write changed only bundleFnv1a64 and bundleBytes in the four baselines. Workspace nextest 311/311; audit:set-categories, audit:export-integrity, audit:dataset-roster, validate:converter and lint:py pass.

crates/app/src/archetype_convert.rs: refit_pieces replaces drop_unfit_pieces; a refused set piece goes through convert_piece and counterpart: an archetype set (category ato) is ranked among its own archetype's sets of the same rarity by bin_order, and becomes the set at the same rank among the new power's archetype category; the piece keeps its number, attunement, craft level and booster (Enhancement::io_set). No order on any set involved, or no set in that position: taken out and listed as before. The report gains converted (from, to, pieces) and reshaped (a piece whose aspects differ). No uniqueness check: the original was legal and the mapping is one-to-one with piece numbers kept. Tests on fixtures rather than the owner's file, which stays out of the repo: tanker_archetype_sets_become_the_brutes (charnel: Death Shroud's Superior Might of the Tanker becomes Superior Brute's Fury and Midnight Grasp's Superior Gauntleted Fist becomes Superior Unrelenting Fury, same piece numbers, attuned, none emptied, nothing reshaped); blaster_archetype_sets_become_the_defenders (sisterachlys: Hailstones' Superior Defiant Barrage becomes Superior Vigilant Assault; Accuracy/Damage/Recharge (Blaster) reported as now Damage/Endurance/Recharge (Defender)); blaster_to_defender_lists_what_could_not_come now expects Category Five's Superior Blaster's Wrath to become Superior Defender's Bastion; an_archetype_set_with_no_recorded_order_is_taken_out (one Brute set's order cleared: neither Tanker set converts, all 12 pieces listed). done_when expected Blaster to Defender to reshape pieces 3 and 4; the data reshapes only those whose mixes differ. Mutations caught: no conversion (3 tests), pairing swapped (3 tests). Equivalent on all real data: ignoring the tier, since the bin lists each regular set right before its Superior twin for every archetype; kept as the rule.

The dialog report has an 'Archetype sets converted to <archetype>'s' section, one line per set ('Superior Gauntleted Fist becomes Superior Unrelenting Fury (6 pieces, same slots)') and one per reshaped piece; 'Left behind' drops a (0) count when only the inherent is listed. Web Q/A on the owner's /home/jiiwii/Desktop/my builds/sonic-kinetic-tank.skif (Tanker, Sonic Aura / Kinetic Melee), converted to Brute: the report read Superior Gauntleted Fist becomes Superior Unrelenting Fury and Superior Might of the Tanker becomes Superior Brute's Fury, 6 pieces each, with no enhancements taken out; after Convert the header read Brute, Kinetic Melee / Sonic Aura, and the build the app saved held Smashing_Blow with superior_unrelenting_fury pieces 1-6 attuned and Total_Focus (Concentrated Strike) with superior_brutes_fury 1-6 attuned, and no Tanker set anywhere; the powers panel screenshot shows Concentrated Strike at L30 with its six pieces. Console errors none. Not checked: phones (no layout change beyond report lines), iPhone.

title: Make the By power list easy to scan
thesis: The set bonus finder's By power list reads as a table: each chosen bonus has its own column so amounts line up, the cost is a short coloured badge in a fixed column, and a bonus's colour says how much Rule-of-5 room is left, so the cheapest useful place stands out without reading every row.
body:
Asked for 2026-10-30, owner: 'can we think of a way to make the By Power list easier to visually parse'. Screenshots of the list on charnel.txt (Energy resistance and Recharge) showed: every row the same weight; the cost a sentence at the far right ('Replaces Superior Blistering Cold' reads like 'Needs 3 more slots and replaces Accuracy IO'); both bonuses stacked in one cell so amounts don't line up; 4/5 and 0/5 drawn alike; with Every set on, power names repeat. Decided 2026-10-30, owner: the bonus-columns layout (offered beside sections-by-cost and cards-by-power), with headroom colour.

The view is ByPowerView and RouteRow in crates/app/src/panels/set_bonus_finder.rs; the rows come from crate::bonus_by_power::routes, whose order does not change here.

Out of scope: grouping by power when Every set is on (the cards-by-power option); changing the order or the costs.

says: The By power list is a table: power, set, one column per chosen bonus (amount and pieces), and a cost badge (Fits, Swap n, +n slots, Slotted); what a swap would replace sits on a dimmer second line.
done_when: In the web app (qa-check), on charnel.txt with Energy resistance and Recharge chosen, a header row names both bonuses, each row's amounts sit under their own header, a set granting only one bonus leaves the other cell empty, and the badges read Swap 1 and +3 slots where the old text said Replaces ... and Needs 3 more slots.

says: Each bonus amount shows the build's Rule-of-5 room for that value: plain while there is room, amber for the fifth and last useful copy, struck through past it.
done_when: In the web app, charnel.txt with Energy resistance: the +2.25% cells (4 of 5 held) are amber, +3% cells (0 of 5) plain; with Hold resistance the +10% cells (5 of 5) are struck through, each with a title saying why.

evidence: crates/app/src/panels/set_bonus_finder.rs: the By power list has a header row (Power, Set, one column per chosen bonus named like its chip, Cost) and RouteRow renders one BonusCell per chosen bonus plus a cost badge (Fits, Swap n, +n slots, Slotted; the full sentence moved to the badge's title) and a dimmer 'Takes out ...' line under the row. app.css: one grid template for header and rows, every track a share of the width so separate rows align; the bonus count rides in --bonus-cols; the header sticks to the top of the finder's scroller (overflow: clip on the table, top: -10px for the finder's padding, found when the first sticky try left a sliver of row showing). Web Q/A on charnel.txt with Energy resistance and Recharge: header read POWER SET ENERGY RESISTANCE RECHARGE OFFENSE COST; Smite row '+2.25% 2pc' under Energy and '+6.25% 4pc' under Recharge, badge Swap 1, 'Takes out Superior Blistering Cold'; badges further down read Swap 4, +3 slots, +4 slots, +5 slots where the old text said Replaces ... and Needs n more slots; 14 cells empty (a dash) where a set grants one bonus only; the header stayed in view after scrolling. app nextest 148/148, lint and fmt clean.

BonusCell draws five pips for the copies held of that value and a state: plain with room, is-last (the theme's heat colour) when 4 are held, is-spent (ember, struck through) at 5 or more, each with a title. Web Q/A on charnel.txt: with Energy resistance the +2.25% cells (4 of 5 held) were amber, 5 such cells, titled 'You hold 4 copies of +2.25%; this would be the last that counts', +3% cells plain; with Hold resistance, Taunt's Perfect Zinger +3.75% cell was struck through in red, titled 'You already hold 5 copies of +3.75%; another grants nothing', the row greyed as before. done_when named the +10% Hold cells; the list's best-per-power rows show Taunt's +3.75% as the spent value, the one the build holds five of among the offered sets.

A container query on the table (bonus-routes, max-width 560px) folds each row: no header, power and its cost badge on the first line, then the set, then each amount with its bonus's name (bonus-cell__label shown only when folded), then the Takes out line. It answers to the panel's own width, so a narrow floating panel on desktop folds too. Pixel 7 (Chromium, touch): table scrollWidth 368 equal to clientWidth 368, no sideways scroll; Smite row read 'Smite L1 · 6 slots / Swap 1 / RARE Cloud Senses +12 other sets / Energy resistance +2.25% 2pc / Recharge offense +6.25% 4pc / Takes out Superior Blistering Cold', amber pips on the Energy line. Not checked: iPhone.
